observations: For partially out-of-range writes, Icarus retains the valid in-range bytes; this installed Verilator build leaves the entire destination slice zero.
For partially out-of-range reads, Icarus retains the valid high bytes and reports X for the out-of-range suffix; this installed Verilator build returns an entirely zero word.
Bounded bytewise writes preserve the expected four-, five- and three-byte tails under both simulators.
implication: A portable ML-DSA testbench must capture all valid signature bytes and explicitly construct valid input bytes without relying on partially out-of-range accesses. This observation does not justify dropping tail comparisons, replacing expected values, or claiming that the DUT passed.
limits: This is a tiny synthetic language/tool behavior diagnostic, not a full ML-DSA run.
It does not establish behavior of other Verilator releases or an independent language-standard conformance finding.
The accompanying ML-DSA baseline failure and corrected full-run results must be reported separately.
